transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-02
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jon Rhodes (IT), Lina Park (Finance), Aisha Patel (Security), Marco Chen (Procurement), Priya Singh (Legal)

Summary: Quick triage on KMS rotation, SSO rollout timeline, billing export automation, and vendor access review. Agree to share diagrams and runbooks and reconvene next week.

[00:00:00] Jon: Okay, everyone, thanks for jumping on. Agenda is short - KMS rotation, SSO rollout, billing export, vendor access. If anyone needs to add something, say now.
[00:00:22] Lina: Quick note - finance had a question about field mappings in the new billing export, I can show example later.
[00:00:35] Aisha: And security wants confirmation on KMS rotation windows - we need a maintenance window that doesn't break Dedicated jobs.
[00:00:50] Jon: Right, that's the main ask. We're aiming for a rolling rotation with 24-hour overlap. I'll explain how the key aliases work.
[00:01:12] Marco: Also procurement needs to know if any vendor-managed keys are in scope - ex: backups on GCS using customer-managed keys.
[00:01:30] Aisha: Good point, Marco - we flagged Google Cloud KMS and AWS KMS for the top vendors. We should document which services use platform KMS vs customer-managed.
[00:01:50] Priya: For legal, also want to ensure rotation schedule and audit logs are included in the SOC2 artifacts.
[00:02:05] Jon: Absolutely. We'll capture audit log retention and rotation proofs.
[00:02:20] Jon: (clears throat) KMS details: current process - keys rotate quarterly, but we had one missed rotation in March because of an infra job that timed out. We're proposing to move to monthly rotations for a subset of keys and keep others quarterly. The monthly ones are high-sensitivity: signing, token encryption.
[00:02:50] Aisha: Is monthly going to increase operational risk? I mean, more rotations could bump up the chance of a mismatch.
[00:03:05] Jon: There's more complexity but we can mitigate with alias layering - add new key, switch alias after verification, and keep previous key for 48 hours. The KV cache on serving side will gracefully fetch new keys, but there might be transient failures in rare edge cases.
[00:03:28] Lina: Will that affect billing exports or any downstream ETL? We had one job that choked when credentials rotated unexpectedly.
[00:03:40] Jon: Good call. We'll coordinate with the ETL owners. For billing export, we'll add an intermediate service account that has long-lived creds to pull CSVs, so rotation doesn't break it.
[00:03:55] Marco: Sounds good, long-lived creds for the export service only, with tight RBAC. We'll also rotate that service account quarterly.
[00:04:10] Aisha: Please document who has access to that service account. Action item for procurement + security.
[00:04:20] Jon: Noted.

[00:05:00] Jon: Next - SSO/SAML rollout. Lina, where are we on finance side?
[00:05:12] Lina: We've tested SAML with Okta in staging; SSO flows look good. A couple of issues: our attribute mapping for groups isn't coming through in one of the attributes - sometimes it's role vs roles naming inconsistency.
[00:05:35] Jon: That's the common hit - Okta sends groups as "roles" for some apps and "group" for others. We'll add a normalize layer in the auth service to accept both.
[00:05:50] Aisha: Also, we need to ensure SCIM provisioning is only enabled for certain orgs. We don't want blanket provisioning until we validate group mapping.
[00:06:05] Jon: Agreed. For rollout plan: stage > limited pilot (finance + two eng teams) > org-wide. Target pilot week of 2026-05-18.
[00:06:20] Lina: Pilot works for us. We'll inform payroll and vendor billing teams.

[00:07:10] Jon: Billing export automation - Lina, you mentioned a spec. Walk us through required fields.
[00:07:22] Lina: We need: invoice_id, cost_center, product_line, usage_start, usage_end, token_count, embedding_units, currency, total_amount, breakdown by model. Some of the model names get mangled in the export, e.g., 'redwood-gen-v1' shows as 'redwood g v one' sometimes because of the old mapping table.
[00:07:52] Jon: Yeah, that's a legacy mapping. We'll normalize model names at export time and add a model_id column to be deterministic.
[00:08:05] Marco: Also want a monthly summary row for budget tracking. Could be helpful for forecasting.
[00:08:15] Lina: Yes, and sample CSV please, with a header row and a separate mapping file.
[00:08:22] Jon: I'll produce an example and push to the shared drive.

[00:09:10] Aisha: Vendor access review - we ran an initial report, there are ~14 vendor accounts with IAM roles higher than needed. We should do a cleanup and request proof of last-use for each.
[00:09:28] Marco: We'll ping procurement to get contract owners to confirm access. For cloud vendors like GCP and AWS, we'll ask for a service list and justification.
[00:09:42] Priya: From legal, if any vendor holds PII or billing data, we need the DPA attached. Also check subprocessors list.
[00:09:55] Jon: Good. Let's plan a vendor access sweep - schedule in the week of 2026-05-11.

[00:10:30] Jon: Quick note on backups: recent restore drills passed, but we found two encrypted snapshots that referenced an old KMS key alias. Aisha, did we miss that in rotation?
[00:10:45] Aisha: That was from a legacy backup job. We'll run a reconciliation and re-encrypt those snapshots with newest key.
[00:10:55] Jon: Please add to action items.

[00:11:40] Jon: Any blockers from anyone?
[00:11:50] Lina: Finance needs the first sample export by 2026-05-06 to validate ingestion into Netsuite and our dashboard.
[00:11:58] Jon: We'll hit that.
[00:12:10] Marco: Procurement needs the vendor-invoice mapping to be accurate before we finalize PO changes. I'll take that on.

[00:13:00] Aisha: On SOC2 artifacts - Priya, can you confirm what level of documentation is preferred? We're thinking: rotation proof (KMS), SSO config screenshots, vendor access attestation, and change access logs.
[00:13:15] Priya: That list is good. Also include the third-party penetration test report and an attestation for incident response. We'll need dates on all items.
[00:13:30] Jon: We'll gather timestamps and export logs.

[00:14:40] Jon: I want to call out one small technical caveat: the serving runtime (redwood runtime) uses a KV cache that keeps a reference to the key fingerprint for a short TTL. During immediate rotations there's a 30-90 second window where cold start requests may rekey; that could surface as 5xx in older clients. We're planning to extend the alias grace window to 48 hours to be safe.
[00:15:05] Aisha: Ok, please add that to runbook. Also ensure we have rollback steps if we see error spikes.
[00:15:20] Jon: Will do.

[00:16:00] Lina: One more finance ask - can we tag billing lines by environment: staging vs production. Right now they get co-mingled.
[00:16:12] Jon: We can add an environment column. It requires minor changes in reporting pipeline but doable.
[00:16:25] Marco: Prefer explicit env tag, yes.

[00:17:00] Jon: Action recap so far: Aisha KMS calendar, Lina sample CSV, Jon SSO runbook + model name normalization, Marco vendor mapping, Priya confirm SOC2 item list. Anything to add?
[00:17:20] Aisha: Also I'll share the KMS architecture diagram showing alias layering and rotation steps.
[00:17:30] Jon: Great.

[00:18:40] Jon: Quick question on emergency rotations - what is the approved out-of-band procedure? If a key is compromised, do we do immediate alias swap or isolate service?
[00:18:55] Priya: Legal recommends immediate containment plus notification to affected customers if there is any chance of data exposure. But we need the IR playbook steps.
[00:19:08] Aisha: Our playbook says: 1) Revoke the key, 2) switch aliases to backup, 3) run verification jobs, 4) notify stakeholders. We'll draft the timeline and thresholds.
[00:19:22] Jon: Okay, make sure to annotate which rotations require customer notice.

[00:20:10] Lina: On the billing side, are we okay to add model_id as a fixed slug rather than human-readable names? That will help downstream analytics.
[00:20:22] Jon: Yes model_id plus a friendly name column. We'll version the mapping file to avoid drift.

[00:21:45] Marco: A small procurement ask - can security confirm the minimum required IAM for the billing export service account? We want to lock it down to minimal permissions.
[00:21:58] Aisha: We'll propose a role with read-only billing + read credentials for buckets, no write. We'll share the exact policy.

[00:23:00] Jon: Anything else on compliance or audits?
[00:23:10] Priya: We want to schedule a dry run for evidence collection for SOC2 - maybe two weeks after these artifacts land. So target the week of 2026-05-25.
[00:23:25] Aisha: Sounds good. We'll aim to have docs in by 2026-05-15 to give you time.

[00:24:40] Jon: Quick operational note - we're deprecating an old S3 bucket used by finance that's been orphaned. We'll need cross-team approval to delete.
[00:24:55] Lina: Please hold off until finance has pulled the last 6 months' of data.
[00:25:05] Jon: Will do.

[00:26:30] Marco: Minor item - vendor invoices sometimes reference the wrong cost center. Can we add a reconciliation column in the export to map invoice -> cost_center?
[00:26:45] Lina: Yes, that helps our GL matching.

[00:28:00] Jon: Ok, nearing the end - action items review. (reads items) The only open question is pilot date for SSO which we set as week of 2026-05-18 - Lina to confirm exact day.
[00:28:30] Lina: I'll confirm by tomorrow.

[00:29:10] Aisha: I'll also post the KMS diagram to the security confluence page and tag procurement.

[00:30:00] Jon: Anything else?
[00:30:10] Marco: Nothing from procurement.
[00:30:20] Priya: All good from legal.

[00:31:00] Jon: Thanks, everyone. I'll send the notes and attach the export example when done.
[00:31:12] Lina: Thanks.
[00:31:15] Aisha: Thanks all.
[00:31:20] The meeting wraps up; recorded end ~15:45 UTC.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had a few phonetic errors around model names and 'KV cache' was sometimes transcribed as 'K V catch' and 'SSO' occasionally as 'S S O'. Speaker labels auto-assigned in places.
summary: Internal cross-functional sync covering KMS rotation cadence, SSO/SAML pilot plan, billing export schema and model normalization, vendor access review, SOC2 artifact collection, and next steps to deliver diagrams and sample exports.
